locked_scene_function: A needs B to reveal who changed a report; B needs A to stop treating B as a subordinate witness. Scene must end with limited cooperation and a new condition, not friendship.
variant_a_without_pair_state: A and B exchange witty suspicion, summarize known facts and end with A saying they should work together. No tactic changes when resistance appears; status remains implicit; withheld fact has no behavioral consequence.
variant_b_with_pair_state: A begins by demanding the name; B refuses and instead asks who will own the accusation. A tries procedural authority; B cites the prior time A used B's statement without warning. A switches tactic and offers B control over when the evidence is released. B gives the location of the altered report but withholds the editor's identity pending that condition. The scene ends with bounded cooperation and a changed power arrangement.
conclusion: The pair-state card improves the probability that dialogue functions as action because resistance triggers tactic change and a measurable scene-state delta. It is not a prose-style template and does not replace character voice work.
cannot_prove: Does not establish reader preference or human naturalism in a specific manuscript.
